verses.mystical_translation: O the Living Presence, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.
Have mercy upon me, O the Living Presence; for I am weak: O the Living Presence, heal me; for my bones are vexed.
my whole being is also sore vexed: but thou, O the Living Presence, how long?
Return, O the Living Presence, deliver my whole being: oh save me for thy mercies’ sake.
For in death there is no remembrance of you; in Sheol who will give you thanks?
I am weary with my groaning; all the night make I my bed to swim; I water my couch with my tears.
Contemplatively, this verse gives voice to the longing that violence, deceit, domination, and fear lose their power; it is not a directive against human enemies.
Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity; for the Living Presence hath heard the voice of my weeping.
the Living Presence hath heard my supplication; the Living Presence will receive my prayer.
Contemplatively, this verse gives voice to the longing that violence, deceit, domination, and fear lose their power; it is not a directive against human enemies.

contemplative_note: Tears themselves become a form of prayer when speech is exhausted.
safety_note: Illness and emotional suffering are not evidence of divine punishment, weak faith, or moral failure.
